title: Quantized topological invariant of symmetry-projected Gibbs states
abstract: We study Gibbs states projected onto the symmetric sector of contractible one-form symmetries. In a three-dimensional cluster-model interpolation, this projection stabilizes symmetry-protected topological and projected-paramagnetic phases, both sharply distinct from thermal disorder. A flux-twisted membrane invariant distinguishes these three phases by the values $-1,+1,0$, respectively. These values are exact on the endpoint, self-dual, zero-temperature, and infinite-temperature lines; elsewhere their quantization requires positive spatial-sheet, winding-line, and interface tensions. Quantum Monte Carlo supports the quantization through tension diagnostics and direct finite-size estimates.
summary: The authors study symmetry-projected Gibbs states in a 3D cluster model to characterize the resulting phase diagram. They introduce a quantized topological invariant, the flux-twisted membrane index, capable of distinguishing between topologically ordered, paramagnetically ordered, and disordered phases. The methodology combines theoretical analysis with advanced Quantum Monte Carlo simulations.
main_problem: The study investigates how projecting Gibbs states onto symmetric sectors stabilizes topological phases at finite temperatures, aiming to determine if this projection induces a phase transition where none existed before.
main_result: A flux-twisted membrane index distinguishes three distinct phases (SPT, projected-paramagnetic, and disordered) with quantized values of $-1, +1,$ and $0$. The phase diagram exhibits continuous transitions and a self-dual first-order line.
method: The analysis combines theoretical derivations involving partition function ratios and symmetry projectors with extensive Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations on 3D tori.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a three-dimensional cluster-model interpolation Hamiltonian $H(s)$ that smoothly transitions between a Symmetry-Protected Topological (SPT) state and a trivial paramagnet. The analysis focuses on the projected Gibbs states defined by specific symmetry projectors ($\mathcal{P}_{loc}$ or $\mathcal{P}_+$).
key_observables: Flux-twisted membrane index ($I$), free-energy splittings ($F_\Sigma(s, T)$), and tension diagnostics (spatial-sheet, winding-line, interface tensions).
important_parameters: The interpolation parameter $s \in [0, 1]$, temperature $T$, and lattice size $L$. Critical values include $T_{I} \approx 1.3133$ for the endpoint mapping.
main_assumptions: Quantization away from specific limits requires positive spatial-sheet, winding-line, and interface tensions; theoretical derivations rely on assumptions about sector asymptotics (Hypothesis H).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the finite-regulator estimate of the projected phase diagram showing three distinct regions separated by continuous and first-order lines. Other figures detail the geometry involving noncontractible cycles.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical context via symmetry projection, derives a topological index ($I$), calculates this index using QMC on finite lattices, and maps out the resulting phase diagram structure across varying parameters $s$ and $T$.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete numerical evidence for how imposing global symmetries (via projection) can stabilize exotic quantum phases at non-zero temperatures, which is a key topic in modern condensed matter theory.
